errors.english: it is conditioned by the (adhisthana) blessing or transformative power of the object or the sense organ
errors.why: The object or the sense organ is what is affected by supernatural power (adhiṣṭhāna); the power does not belong to the object or sense organ.

fix.find: it is conditioned by the (adhisthana) blessing or transformative power of the object or the sense organ
fix.replace: the object or the sense organ is conditioned by (adhisthana) blessing or transformative power

errors.english: Their reversal is the non-existence of non-perception.
errors.why: Their absence is the non-existence established by non-perception; 'non-existence of non-perception' would mean perception, the opposite.

fix.find: Their reversal is the non-existence of non-perception.
fix.replace: Their absence is the non-existence that consists in non-perception.

errors.english: Since it is possible for a cause to exist without the result, this also thoroughly expresses the answer to the claim that
errors.why: 'Since a cause may exist without its effect' belongs to the opponent's objection being answered, not to the commentator's own reasoning.

note: Follows the argument in outline, but it misreads who is affected by adhiṣṭhāna, turns the definition of absence-by-non-perception into its opposite, and gives part of the opponent's objection as the commentator's own reasoning.
A faithful rendering of the argument and of the Akṣayamatinirdeśa quotation; the remaining wording points are defensible.

errors.english: you will remember me, who am free from worldly existence
errors.why: 'Free from existence' (srid med) describes the addressee, who will have attained awakening, not the speaker asking to be remembered.
This is the Jātakamālā narrative opening 'tradition has it' (tadyathānuśrūyate), not the sūtra formula evaṃ mayā śrutam.

note: The verses and the frame of the new story are sound; a referent in the hermit's verse is misplaced, and the story's opening uses the sūtra formula.

errors.english: refers to the two aspects of the object and the cognition related to the object
errors.why: The phrase qualifies the conditioned entity as able to accomplish, without depending on anything else, the two kinds of function (one concerning the object, one concerning cognition); it is not a definition of substance as 'two aspects'.

errors.english: Those things established as the basis for the phenomena and subject are the second category.
errors.why: The second category is the properties and property-bearers that take the qualities as their basis, not the basis of the properties.

note: A generally sound rendering of the substance/quality discussion and of the reply to the Vaiśeṣika, with two misparsed clauses in the definitions.

errors.english: Likewise, when birth occurs through the linking of another moment of similar kind, this is purely a negation.
errors.why: Destruction as cessation of the continuum is a mere negation OF the arising of another similar moment; the English makes the arising itself the negation.

fix.find: Likewise, when birth occurs through the linking of another moment of similar kind, this is purely a negation.
fix.replace: Likewise, it is purely a negation of the birth that occurs through the linking of another moment of similar kind.

note: A careful and technically competent rendering of the two kinds of destruction and of contradiction; one clause has its relation inverted.

errors.english: this object appearing from the primary word
errors.why: gtso bo here is pradhāna, the Sāṃkhya primal matter, the standard example of a word whose referent may lack a real material cause, not 'primary word'.

note: The argument and the summary verses are rendered soundly; the key example term pradhāna is lost.

errors.english: and act like a spiritual teacher or a lord toward others.
errors.why: The sentence, completed on the next side with ཁྱད་དུ་གསད་པར་མི་བྱའོ, says one should NOT treat others with contempt as if one were their guru or lord; the English completes it as a positive instruction.

fix.find: and act like a spiritual teacher or a lord toward others.
fix.replace: and not treat others with contempt, as if one were their guru or lord.

errors.english: Should not be despised in this world,
errors.why: The verse says the person should do what is not censured in this world (and what brings happiness in the next); it is the deed, not the person, that is uncensured.

fix.find: Should not be despised in this world,
fix.replace: Should do what is not censured in this world,

note: The buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son illustrations are well rendered, but the root verse is misconstrued and the closing instruction is inverted.
A faithful rendering of a dense commentary on waking and dream cognition and on the cognition of absence.

errors.english: it is not impossible for both of those two aspects, being omniscient and being a speaker, to exist together
errors.why: What is impossible is either of the two kinds of contradiction between omniscience and being a speaker; the lemma 'impossible' refers to the contradiction, not to the two qualities, as the English's 'being a speaker and being omniscient are impossible' wrongly states.

fix.find: it is not impossible for both of those two aspects, being omniscient and being a speaker, to exist together
fix.replace: neither of those two kinds of contradiction is possible between being omniscient and being a speaker

errors.english: the non-inference of a second entity
errors.why: mi dmigs pa is non-perception (anupalabdhi), not non-inference.

fix.find: the non-inference of a second entity
fix.replace: the non-perception of a second entity

errors.english: we do not see any contradiction between them
errors.why: The text says that when omniscience is present, the cessation of speech (ldog pa) is not observed, which is the test for contradiction by mutual exclusion; it does not directly say 'no contradiction'.

errors.english: In order to show that there is also doubt regarding the exclusion of passion and so forth in one who teaches
errors.why: The case is the inference that someone is possessed of passion etc. (rāgādimattva, because he speaks), whose exclusion is doubtful; སྟོན་པ here is 'showing/proving', not 'one who teaches'.

note: The sandigdhavyatireka argument is broadly followed, but the opening lemma is misreported and key logical terms are slipped (non-perception, cessation, the probandum).
A faithful rendering of the word-by-word commentary on the tigress story.
